================================================================================
JAMMU AND KASHMIR STATE BOARD OF SCHOOL EDUCATION (JKBOSE)
HIGHER SECONDARY EXAMINATION PART-II (CLASS 12TH) - OFFICIAL QUESTION PAPER
================================================================================
EXAM PAPER TITLE : JK-BOSE-CLASS-12-CHEMISTRY-9318-A-2011
SUBJECT          : CHEMISTRY (CLASS 12TH)
CLASS / LEVEL    : Class 12TH
EXAMINATION YEAR : 2011
SERIES / SET     : SET A
QUESTION CODE    : 9318
MAXIMUM MARKS    : 70 MARKS
TIME ALLOWED     : 3 HOURS
================================================================================

GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  (1) All questions are compulsory. There are 14 questions in this paper.
  (2) Section A comprises Q. 1 to Q. 6 of 1 mark each.
  (3) Section B comprises Q. 7 to Q. 9 of 2 marks each.
  (4) Section C comprises Q. 10 to Q. 12 of 3 marks each.
  (5) Section D comprises Q. 13 to Q. 14 of 5 marks each with internal choice.
  (6) Calculators are not permitted. Log tables can be used.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

================================================================================
SECTION A : OBJECTIVE & VERY SHORT ANSWER
[Q. 01 to Q. 06 [6 Marks]]
================================================================================

Q.01 [1 Mark] (Solutions - Colligative Properties):
     Which of the following aqueous solutions will exhibit the highest boiling point elevation?

     (A) 0.1 M Glucose
     (B) 0.1 M NaCl
     (C) 0.1 M BaCl₂
     (D) 0.1 M Urea

Q.02 [1 Mark] (Electrochemistry):
     The unit of molar conductivity (Λₘ) is:

     (A) S cm² mol⁻¹
     (B) S cm⁻¹ mol⁻¹
     (C) S⁻¹ cm² mol
     (D) Ω cm mol⁻¹

Q.03 [1 Mark] (Chemical Kinetics):
     For a first order reaction, the time required for 99.9% completion is how many times the half-life period (t₁/₂)?

     (A) 2 times
     (B) 5 times
     (C) 10 times
     (D) 100 times

Q.04 [1 Mark] (Coordination Compounds):
     The IUPAC name of the complex compound [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]Cl₂ is:

     (A) Pentaamminechlorocobalt(III) chloride
     (B) Pentaamminechlorocobalt(II) chloride
     (C) Chloropentaamminecobalt(III) dichloride
     (D) Cobalt(III) pentaamminechloride

Q.05 [1 Mark] (d- and f-Block Elements):
     What is Lanthanoid Contraction and what is its main chemical consequence on 4d and 5d transition elements?

Q.06 [1 Mark] (Biomolecules):
     What is the primary difference between DNA and RNA with respect to their sugar moiety and pyrimidine bases?

================================================================================
SECTION B : SHORT ANSWER TYPE - I
[Q. 07 to Q. 09 [6 Marks]]
================================================================================

Q.07 [2 Marks] (Electrochemistry - Kohlrausch Law):
     State Kohlrausch's Law of Independent Migration of Ions and write its application in determining the limiting molar conductivity of weak electrolytes.

Q.08 [2 Marks] (Haloalkanes & Haloarenes):
     Explain why haloarenes are extremely less reactive towards Nucleophilic Substitution Reactions as compared to haloalkanes.

Q.09 [2 Marks] (Amines):
     How will you distinguish between primary, secondary, and tertiary aliphatic amines using the Hinsberg Test (Benzenesulfonyl chloride)?

================================================================================
SECTION C : SHORT ANSWER TYPE - II
[Q. 10 to Q. 12 [9 Marks]]
================================================================================

Q.10 [3 Marks] (Solutions - Nernst Equation):
     Calculate the EMF of the following Galvanic cell at 298 K:
     Mg(s) | Mg²⁺(0.001 M) || Cu²⁺(0.0001 M) | Cu(s)
     Given: E°(Mg²⁺/Mg) = -2.37 V, E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V, [R = 8.314 J/K·mol, F = 96500 C/mol].

Q.11 [3 Marks] (Coordination Chemistry):
     On the basis of Crystal Field Theory (CFT), explain why [CoF₆]³⁻ is a paramagnetic high-spin complex whereas [Co(CN)₆]³⁻ is a diamagnetic low-spin complex.

Q.12 [3 Marks] (Organic Named Reactions):
     Write chemical equations illustrating the following named reactions:
     (a) Reimer-Tiemann Reaction
     (b) Williamson Ether Synthesis
     (c) Cannizzaro Reaction

================================================================================
SECTION D : LONG ANSWER QUESTIONS (CHOICE)
[Q. 13 to Q. 14 [10 Marks]]
================================================================================

Q.13 [5 Marks] (Aldehydes, Ketones & Carboxylic Acids):
     (a) How will you convert:
         (i) Ethanal to But-2-enal (Aldol Condensation)
         (ii) Benzoic acid to m-Nitrobenzoic acid
         (iii) Propanone to Propene
     (b) Give a simple chemical test to distinguish between:
         (i) Acetaldehyde and Benzaldehyde (Tollens' vs Fehling's)
         (ii) Pentan-2-one and Pentan-3-one (Iodoform test)

     ----------------------------------------------------------------------
     OR
     (a) Explain the mechanism of Nucleophilic Addition reaction of HCN to an Aldehyde/Ketone.
     (b) Why are carboxylic acids more acidic than phenols?
     (c) What is Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction? Give a chemical equation.

Q.14 [5 Marks] (Chemical Kinetics & Solutions):
     (a) Define rate constant (k). Derive the integrated rate equation for a first-order reaction and write the expression for its half-life.
     (b) The rate constant of a first-order reaction doubles when the temperature increases from 300 K to 310 K. Calculate the activation energy (Eₐ) of the reaction. [R = 8.314 J/K·mol].

     ----------------------------------------------------------------------
     OR
     (a) State Raoult's Law for a solution containing non-volatile solute. Derive the relationship between relative lowering of vapour pressure and molar mass of solute.
     (b) Define osmotic pressure. Why is the osmotic pressure method considered superior to other colligative property methods for determining the molecular mass of polymers and proteins?

================================================================================
[END OF QUESTION PAPER - JK-BOSE-CLASS-12-CHEMISTRY-9318-A-2011]
Official Source Archive: https://www.jkboseonline.com/jk-bose-class-12.html
================================================================================

JAMMU AND KASHMIR STATE BOARD OF SCHOOL EDUCATION (JKBOSE)
HIGHER SECONDARY EXAMINATION PART-II (CLASS 12TH) - OFFICIAL QUESTION PAPER
================================================================================
EXAM PAPER TITLE : JK-BOSE-CLASS-12-PHYSICS-9317-A-2011
SUBJECT          : PHYSICS (CLASS 12TH)
CLASS / LEVEL    : Class 12TH
EXAMINATION YEAR : 2011
SERIES / SET     : SET A
QUESTION CODE    : 9317
MAXIMUM MARKS    : 70 MARKS
TIME ALLOWED     : 3 HOURS
================================================================================

GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  (1) All questions are compulsory. There are 15 questions in this paper.
  (2) Section A comprises Q. 1 to Q. 6 of 1 mark each.
  (3) Section B comprises Q. 7 to Q. 9 of 2 marks each.
  (4) Section C comprises Q. 10 to Q. 13 of 3 marks each.
  (5) Section D comprises Q. 14 to Q. 15 of 5 marks each with internal choice.
  (6) Logarithmic tables may be used. Electronic calculators are strictly forbidden.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

================================================================================
SECTION A : OBJECTIVE & VERY SHORT ANSWER
[Q. 01 to Q. 06 [6 Marks]]
================================================================================

Q.01 [1 Mark] (Electrostatics - Gauss Law):
     An electric dipole of dipole moment p is placed in a uniform electric field E at an angle of 90°. The torque acting on the dipole is:

     (A) pE
     (B) 0
     (C) -pE
     (D) pE/2

Q.02 [1 Mark] (Current Electricity - Drift Velocity):
     When a potential difference V is applied across a conductor of length L, the drift velocity of free electrons is proportional to:

     (A) V and L
     (B) V and 1/L
     (C) 1/V and L
     (D) √V and L

Q.03 [1 Mark] (Electromagnetic Induction):
     Lenz’s law of electromagnetic induction is a consequence of the law of conservation of:

     (A) Charge
     (B) Momentum
     (C) Energy
     (D) Mass

Q.04 [1 Mark] (Wave Optics):
     In Young’s double slit experiment, if the separation between the slits is halved and the distance between the slits and screen is doubled, the fringe width will:

     (A) Remain unchanged
     (B) Be doubled
     (C) Become four-fold
     (D) Be halved

Q.05 [1 Mark] (Dual Nature of Radiation):
     State how the de Broglie wavelength (λ) of an electron varies with its accelerating potential (V).

Q.06 [1 Mark] (Semiconductors):
     Why is a semiconductor damaged by a strong current, and what is the width of the depletion layer in a forward-biased p-n junction?

================================================================================
SECTION B : SHORT ANSWER TYPE QUESTIONS - I
[Q. 07 to Q. 09 [6 Marks]]
================================================================================

Q.07 [2 Marks] (Current Electricity - Kirchhoff Rules):
     State Kirchhoff's First Rule (Junction Rule) and Second Rule (Loop Rule). Name the conservation principles on which they are based.

Q.08 [2 Marks] (Magnetism - Moving Charges):
     Derive an expression for the force per unit length between two infinitely long straight parallel conductors carrying currents I₁ and I₂ separated by a distance 'd'. Define 1 Ampere.

Q.09 [2 Marks] (Nuclear Physics):
     Define mass defect and binding energy per nucleon. Draw a graph showing the variation of binding energy per nucleon with mass number (A).

================================================================================
SECTION C : SHORT ANSWER TYPE QUESTIONS - II
[Q. 10 to Q. 13 [12 Marks]]
================================================================================

Q.10 [3 Marks] (Ray Optics - Lens Maker Formula):
     Derive the Lens Maker's Formula 1/f = (μ - 1)(1/R₁ - 1/R₂) for a thin double convex lens of radii of curvature R₁ and R₂.

Q.11 [3 Marks] (Alternating Current - LCR Series Circuit):
     An alternating voltage V = V₀ sin(ωt) is applied across a series LCR circuit. Obtain the impedance (Z) using the phasor diagram and find the condition for electrical resonance.

Q.12 [3 Marks] (Photoelectric Effect):
     State Einstein's photoelectric equation. Explain the characteristics of photoelectric emission (threshold frequency, saturation current, and stopping potential).

Q.13 [3 Marks] (Semiconductor Diodes):
     Explain the working of a full-wave rectifier using two junction diodes with a neat circuit diagram. Draw input and output waveforms.

================================================================================
SECTION D : LONG ANSWER TYPE QUESTIONS (CHOICE)
[Q. 14 to Q. 15 [10 Marks]]
================================================================================

Q.14 [5 Marks] (Electrostatics - Capacitance & Gauss Law):
     State Gauss's Law in electrostatics.
     Using Gauss's Law, derive an expression for the electric field intensity due to an infinitely long straight uniformly charged wire.
     A parallel plate capacitor with air between the plates has a capacitance of 8 pF. What will be the capacitance if the distance between the plates is reduced by half and the space between them is filled with a dielectric substance of dielectric constant K = 6?

     ----------------------------------------------------------------------
     OR
     Define electric potential.
     Derive an expression for the electrostatic potential energy of an electric dipole placed in a uniform electric field.
     Derive the formula for the capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor with a dielectric slab inserted between its plates.

Q.15 [5 Marks] (Electromagnetic Induction & AC Generator):
     Explain the principle, construction, and working of an AC Generator with the help of a labelled diagram.
     Derive the expression for the induced alternating EMF generated in the rotating coil.
     State the energy losses occurring in a real transformer and how they can be minimized.

     ----------------------------------------------------------------------
     OR
     State Huygens' Principle of wave optics.
     Using Huygens' wave theory, prove the Laws of Reflection and Laws of Refraction at a plane separating two optical media.
     In Young's double slit experiment using monochromatic light of wavelength 600 nm, 12 fringes are observed in a certain segment of the screen. How many fringes will be observed in the same segment if light of wavelength 400 nm is used?

================================================================================
[END OF QUESTION PAPER - JK-BOSE-CLASS-12-PHYSICS-9317-A-2011]
Official Source Archive: https://www.jkboseonline.com/jk-bose-class-12.html
================================================================================

>>> Title: JK-BOSE-CLASS-12-BIOLOGY-BOTANY-34019-2010 | Year: 2010 | Set: - | Code: 34019

================================================================================
JAMMU AND KASHMIR STATE BOARD OF SCHOOL EDUCATION (JKBOSE)
HIGHER SECONDARY EXAMINATION PART-II (CLASS 12TH) - OFFICIAL QUESTION PAPER
================================================================================
EXAM PAPER TITLE : JK-BOSE-CLASS-12-BIOLOGY-BOTANY-34019-2010
SUBJECT          : BIOLOGY (CLASS 12TH)
CLASS / LEVEL    : Class 12TH
EXAMINATION YEAR : 2010
SERIES / SET     : SET -
QUESTION CODE    : 34019
MAXIMUM MARKS    : 70 MARKS
TIME ALLOWED     : 3 HOURS
================================================================================

GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  (1) The question paper contains two sections: Section A (Botany) and Section B (Zoology).
  (2) Both sections are compulsory and carry 35 marks each.
  (3) Diagrams must be clear and properly labelled.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

================================================================================
SECTION A : BOTANY : ANGIOSPERM REPRODUCTION, GENETICS, AND PLANT BIOTECHNOLOGY
[Q. 01 to Q. 06 [35 Marks]]
================================================================================

Q.01 [1 Mark] (Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants):
     The ploidy level of the Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN) in angiosperms after double fertilization is:

     (A) Haploid (n)
     (B) Diploid (2n)
     (C) Triploid (3n)
     (D) Tetraploid (4n)

Q.02 [1 Mark] (Genetics - Molecular Biology):
     Which enzyme synthesizes the RNA primer required during DNA replication?

     (A) DNA Polymerase I
     (B) DNA Primase
     (C) Topoisomerase
     (D) DNA Ligase

Q.03 [2 Marks] (Microbes in Human Welfare):
     Name the biocontrol agents used in organic farming to manage pests without synthetic pesticides.

Q.04 [2 Marks] (Ecosystem):
     Differentiate between standing crop and standing state in an ecosystem.

Q.05 [3 Marks] (Molecular Genetics - Lac Operon):
     Describe the regulation of the Lac Operon model in E. coli in the presence and absence of lactose (inducer).

Q.06 [5 Marks] (Plant Reproduction):
     Describe the development of a female gametophyte (embryo sac) from a functional megaspore in angiosperms with labelled diagrams. What is monosporic development?

     ----------------------------------------------------------------------
     OR
     State Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment.
     Explain with the help of a Punnett square the inheritance of two pairs of contrasting traits (Dihybrid Cross) in Pisum sativum (Pea plant).

================================================================================
SECTION B : ZOOLOGY : HUMAN REPRODUCTION, HEALTH, EVOLUTION, AND ANIMAL BIOTECHNOLOGY
[Q. 07 to Q. 12 [35 Marks]]
================================================================================

Q.07 [1 Mark] (Human Reproduction):
     The hormone responsible for the surge causing ovulation from the Graafian follicle is:

     (A) Progesterone
     (B) Luteinizing Hormone (LH)
     (C) FSH
     (D) Estrogen

Q.08 [1 Mark] (Biotechnology):
     Restriction endonucleases cleave DNA molecules at specific palindromic recognition sequences, creating:

     (A) Sticky ends or blunt ends
     (B) RNA transcripts
     (C) Peptide bonds
     (D) Okazaki fragments

Q.09 [2 Marks] (Reproductive Health):
     Explain what is meant by Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART). Briefly describe IVF-ET and ICSI.

Q.10 [2 Marks] (Human Health and Disease):
     Differentiate between Innate Immunity and Acquired Immunity. Mention two physiological barriers of innate immunity.

Q.11 [3 Marks] (Biotechnology Principles - PCR):
     Explain the three sequential steps involved in Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR): Denaturation, Annealing, and Extension.

Q.12 [5 Marks] (Human Physiology / Evolution):
     Describe the structure of human sperm and explain the process of Spermatogenesis with the help of a schematic diagram.

     ----------------------------------------------------------------------
     OR
     Explain the life cycle of the malarial parasite Plasmodium vivax with a detailed schematic diagram illustrating human host and female Anopheles mosquito stages.

================================================================================
[END OF QUESTION PAPER - JK-BOSE-CLASS-12-BIOLOGY-BOTANY-34019-2010]
Official Source Archive: https://www.jkboseonline.com/jk-bose-class-12.html
================================================================================

     (B) 0
     (C) -pE
     (D) pE/2

Q.02 [1 Mark] (Current Electricity - Drift Velocity):
     When a potential difference V is applied across a conductor of length L, the drift velocity of free electrons is proportional to:

     (A) V and L
     (B) V and 1/L
     (C) 1/V and L
     (D) √V and L

Q.03 [1 Mark] (Electromagnetic Induction):
     Lenz’s law of electromagnetic induction is a consequence of the law of conservation of:

     (A) Charge
     (B) Momentum
     (C) Energy
     (D) Mass

Q.04 [1 Mark] (Wave Optics):
     In Young’s double slit experiment, if the separation between the slits is halved and the distance between the slits and screen is doubled, the fringe width will:

     (A) Remain unchanged
     (B) Be doubled
     (C) Become four-fold
     (D) Be halved

Q.05 [1 Mark] (Dual Nature of Radiation):
     State how the de Broglie wavelength (λ) of an electron varies with its accelerating potential (V).

Q.06 [1 Mark] (Semiconductors):
     Why is a semiconductor damaged by a strong current, and what is the width of the depletion layer in a forward-biased p-n junction?
